newsitem.title: USA: Boeing says Pembroke Capital orders 12 jets.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says Pembroke Capital orders 12 jets.

text.p: Boeing Co said Thursday that Pembroke Capital Ltd of Ireland has ordered eight 737-700s and four 737-300s. Boeing said the orders are valued at about $504 million.
Boeing said deliveries are scheduled to begin in June 1998 and will continue through April 1999.
It said Dublin-based Pembroke was its 25th next-generation 737 customer.
Pembroke founder and president MIchael Dolan said the order represents a significant boost to his company's fleet.
Of the 23 Boeing 737 aircraft now under management by Pembroke, the company owns three 737-300s and one 737-400 which are on lease to Air New Zealand, MAERSK and Air Berlin, it said.
The order for a dozen 737s is Pembroke's first direct purchase of new airplanes from Boeing, it said.
Boeing said that with the Pembroke order, total 737 orders stand at 3,626.
